name_reason: Follows the fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (domain=char growth table accessor). Accurately reflects the body: returns &character_growth_table[idx]. KB (fd2-knowledge struct char_growth_entry, 11-byte stride) confirms this is the per-character growth table. No Ghidra address residue in the name; 0xB stride is a semantic constant (entry size), not an address suffix.
purpose: Leaf accessor returning a pointer to the idx-th 11-byte entry of the character growth table at 0x620A1.
logic_summary: Computes idx * 0xB + 0x620A1 and returns it as a byte pointer (= &data_fd2_battle_character_growth_table[idx].bAP_min, the entry's first field). No side effects, single basic block, __cdecl with one stack arg. The 11-byte entry holds per-stat growth deltas: +0x00 bAP_min, +0x01 bAP_max, +0x02 bDP_min, +0x03 bDP_max, +0x04 bDX_min, +0x05 bDX_max, +0x06 bHP_min, +0x07 bHP_max, +0x08 bMP_min, +0x09 bMP_max, +0x0A spell-learning index (0xFF = none). Callers scale these deltas by character level to derive runtime HP/MP/AP/DP/DX.

params.name: idx
params.semantics: Character/portrait id used as the index into the growth table. All four callers pass a character id (char_id) and then read growth fields (AP/DP/DX/HP/MP min/max). Valid range 0..0x43 (68 entries) per the plate/KB.
params.reason: Not param_1, not address-tainted, and matches its use (a table index). All sibling accessors in table.c (fd2_get_char_base_entry, fd2_get_enemy_data_entry, etc.) uniformly use 'idx' for the index argument; keeping 'idx' preserves file-wide consistency. (char_id would be marginally more descriptive given callers, but does not rise to a needed rename and would break the file's naming pattern.)

returns.semantics: Pointer to the first byte (bAP_min) of character_growth_table[idx]; callers index off this base to read the individual growth-delta fields.

comment_original_issue: Original src comment was correct but terse ('Returns pointer to character_growth_table[idx].'), omitting that idx is a character/portrait id and what the 11-byte entry contains. Augmented to convey parameter meaning and entry semantics, matching the richer Ghidra plate and the fd2-knowledge struct definition.
notes: Minor nuance: fd2-knowledge describes the max-growth fields (XX1) as 'max growth + 1' whereas the Ghidra plate labels them simply 'maximum growth'. This is an interpretation detail of the table data, not a logic issue, and the plate's field naming/purpose remain correct; left the plate unchanged (consistent, not contradictory). Caller fd2_init_runtime_char_from_base_growth confirms growth fields are read at +0/+2/+4/+6/+8 and scaled by level. No emit_action/category metadata applies (leaf accessor already emitted in src/table/table.c).
